Photograph of a dog (Chihuahua?) sitting on a pumpkin in which there is a cow calf, ca.1920. source_metadata_raw: {"imageinfo": {"descriptionshorturl": "https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=136505451", "descriptionurl": "https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Oil_and_Gas_exploration_halted_in_Arctic_National_Wildlife_Refuge,_Alaska.jpg", "extmetadata": {"Artist": {"source": "commons-desc-page", "value": "European Union, Copernicus Sentinel-2 imagery"}, "Attribution": {"hidden": "", "source": "commons-desc-page", "value": "Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2020"}, "Categories": {"hidden": "", "source": "commons-categories", "value": "Kaktovik, Alaska|2020 satellite pictures|Attribution Copernicus|Photographs taken on 2020-07-07|Photos of the United States by Sentinel-2|Copernicus files uploaded by OptimusPrimeBot"}, "Credit": {"source": "commons-desc-page", "value": "Oil and Gas exploration halted in Arctic National Wildlife Refuge, Alaska"}, "ImageDescription": {"source": "commons-desc-page", "value": "The Arctic National Wildlife Refuge (ANWR), located in the very Northeast of Alaska, is the largest national wildlife refuge in the United States. It is home to various species of fauna, including polar bears, moose, and wolves, as well as countless migratory birds from around the world that visit it each year. The region first became a federal protected area in 1960, and the ANWR was established in two decades later, via the Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act. However, the United States Congress deferred the decision regarding management of oil and gas exploration in a coastal plain discussed in section 1002 (referred to as the 1002 area). This area spans about 600,000 ha and — despite its importance as a wildlife habitat — has been a subject of ongoing discussion due to the enormous oil and gas resources it is suspected to contain. No decisions were made regarding oil exploration in the 1002 area until 2017, when a tax legislation that would allow for oil and gas drilling was signed into law. Numerous disputes followed this decision, but in February 2021, all exploration plans are reported to have finally fizzled out due to their lack of measures to ensure protection of the polar bear habitats of the ANWR. This image, acquired by one of the Copernicus Sentinel-2 satellites on 7 July 2020, shows the city of Kaktovik in the 1002 area, around which seismic surveys were planned. Data acquired by Copernicus Sentinel satellites are used operationally to monitor the impact of climate change on the fragile ecosystems in the Arctic."}, "LicenseShortName": {"hidden": "", "source": "commons-desc-page", "value": "Attribution"}, "ObjectName": {"source": "mediawiki-metadata", "value": "Oil and Gas exploration halted in Arctic National Wildlife Refuge, Alaska"}}, "height": 2540, "mime": "image/jpeg", "sha1": "24525e21c6941b14e0b17bcfde521545570fa134", "size": 2834157, "timestamp": "2023-08-27T08:26:18Z", "url": "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/72/Oil_and_Gas_exploration_halted_in_Arctic_National_Wildlife_Refuge%2C_Alaska.jpg?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original", "width": 3508}, "search_page": {"ns": 6, "pageid": 136505451, "size": 2183, "snippet": "lted-arctic-national-wildlife-refuge-alaska URL: https://www.copernicus.eu/system/files/2021-02/image_day/ArcticNationalWildlifeRefuge.jpg determination", "timestamp": "2025-01-25T16:09:26Z", "title": "File:Oil and Gas exploration halted in Arctic National Wildlife Refuge, Alaska.jpg", "wordcount": 80}}

source_metadata_raw: {"imageinfo": {"descriptionshorturl": "https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=151525759", "descriptionurl": "https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Recent_avian_flu_burst_in_the_Antarctic_region_(Copernicus_2023-12-15).jpg", "extmetadata": {"Artist": {"source": "commons-desc-page", "value": "European Union, Copernicus Sentinel-2 imagery"}, "Attribution": {"hidden": "", "source": "commons-desc-page", "value": "Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2023"}, "Categories": {"hidden": "", "source": "commons-categories", "value": "Bird Island, South Georgia|Sentinel-2 images|Attribution Copernicus|Photographs taken on 2023-10-19|2023 satellite pictures|Copernicus files uploaded by OptimusPrimeBot"}, "Credit": {"source": "commons-desc-page", "value": "Recent avian flu burst in the Antarctic region"}, "ImageDescription": {"source": "commons-desc-page", "value": "Bird Island, located in the Antarctic Ocean near South Georgia, serves as critical habitat for numerous species of seabirds and fur seals. In October, the first cases of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) in the Antarctic region were detected on Bird Island. The virus has led to hundreds of fatalities among elephant seals, along with increased mortalities among fur seals, kelp gulls, and brown skuas in various locations. Currently, confirmed avian flu-related deaths have been identified at eight Antarctic sites, while 20 other sites await conclusive test results for suspected cases. The Scientific Committee on Antarctic Research recently warned that the proliferation of this disease is posing a severe threat to wildlife in the region. This image of Bird Island was acquired by one of the Copernicus Sentinel-2 satellites on 19 October 2023. The use of imagery from the Copernicus Sentinel satellites, combined with in situ data, is key in monitoring protected areas and preserving their biodiversity."}, "LicenseShortName": {"hidden": "", "source": "commons-desc-page", "value": "Attribution"}, "ObjectName": {"source": "mediawiki-metadata", "value": "Recent avian flu burst in the Antarctic region (Copernicus 2023-12-15)"}}, "height": 3522, "mime": "image/jpeg", "sha1": "2734e6395832417a85867deffb0da937b0b433c2", "size": 5128292, "timestamp": "2024-08-16T15:17:36Z", "url": "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/90/Recent_avian_flu_burst_in_the_Antarctic_region_%28Copernicus_2023-12-15%29.jpg?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original", "width": 5478}, "search_page": {"ns": 6, "pageid": 151525759, "size": 1652, "snippet": "Attribution English This image of Bird Island was acquired by one of the Copernicus Sentinel-2 satellites on 19 October 2023. determination method or standard:", "timestamp": "2025-01-25T16:12:36Z", "title": "File:Recent avian flu burst in the Antarctic region (Copernicus 2023-12-15).jpg", "wordcount": 66}}

It stretches across all 27 EU Member States, both on land and at sea. The aim of the network is to ensure the long-term survival of Europe's most valuable and threatened species and habitats. It is made up of Special Areas of Conservation (SPC) and Special Protection Areas (SPA) designated under the Habitats Directive and the Birds Directive, the two EU directives that are related to wildlife and nature conservation. The approach to conservation and sustainable use of the Natura 2000 areas does not exclude human activities from the protected sites because it is centred on people working with nature rather than against it. This image captured by one of the two Copernicus Sentinel-2 satellites on 20 September 2020 shows the island of Lefkada, that is one of the seven major Ionian Islands and a group of smaller ionian islands. In this area, two different Natura2000 sites have been designated. One consists of the central and mountainous part of Lefkada and its importance is the consequence on the presence of some important floristic and biogeographical elements. The second site, known as Esoteriko Archipelagos Ioniou (Meganisi, Arkoudi, Atokos, Vromonas), protects the local marine environment including the coasts of smaller islands and islets that are almost all visible in the image. The geomorphology of these islands’ coasts creates various habitats for the marine and land flora and fauna. The pristine waters of the archipelago provide a shelter to important marine predator species on the top of the food chain, as a result the biological richness of the area. The Copernicus Sentinel-2 mission, composed by two twin satellites (Sentinel-2A and Sentinel-2B), provides multispectral data in 13 different spectral bands with a maximum spatial resolution of 10 metres. The conservation and protection of biodiversity is a fundamental activity in protected areas, such as the Samaria National Park, in Greece. The use of data from the Copernicus Sentinel-2 satellites, combined with geodiversity variables, are proving to be fundamental in monitoring the protected areas to ensure the conservation of their biodiversity."}, "LicenseShortName": {"hidden": "", "source": "commons-desc-page", "value": "Attribution"}, "ObjectName": {"source": "mediawiki-metadata", "value": "Ionian Islands, Greece"}}, "height": 2480, "mime": "image/jpeg", "sha1": "ec818609926dcf326f3cfe0feced4371d719cfad", "size": 8894942, "timestamp": "2023-08-24T15:08:35Z", "url": "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/c2/Ionian_Islands%2C_Greece.jpg?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original", "width": 3507}, "search_page": {"ns": 6, "pageid": 136406729, "size": 2784, "snippet": "designated under the Habitats Directive and the Birds Directive, the two EU directives that are related to wildlife and nature conservation.
